newsitem.title: UK: BRAZIL 1996 SUGAR OUTPUT RISES, EXPORTS DOWN - ISO.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL 1996 SUGAR OUTPUT RISES, EXPORTS DOWN - ISO.

text.p: Brazilian sugar production amounted to 14.72 million tonnes raw value in 1996, up from the 13.83 million recorded for 1995, the International Sugar Organization (ISO) said on Friday.
But sugar exports for 1996 were lower than in the previous year, reaching 5.31 million tonnes after 6.30 million, the ISO said in its July Statistical Bulletin.
Nigeria took the lion's share of the 1996 exports with 587,778 tonnes, roughly double the 290,431 tonnes which it imported in 1995.
Russia also imported significant quantities of Brazilian sugar in the year, more whites than raws. But the Russian purchases were half the amount taken in 1995.
It imported 500,345 tonnes from Brazil in 1996, of which 160,100 were raws and 340,245 were whites, compared with a total 1.04 million tonnes in 1995.

Brazil's annual sugar consumption rose to 8.49 million tonnes in 1996 from 8.23 million, the ISO said. Ending stocks totalled 3.37 million tonnes in December 1996, compared with 2.46 million in December 1995.
